answer: I was so excited to get my driver's license, but when I tried to turn right, the car slipped and I almost crashed into the curb. I was scared and felt really stupid. Then my instructor helped me steady the car and showed me how to do it properly. It was tough, but I kept trying and eventually got it right. I feel much more confident now.

I told them I was going to the club, but they didn’t believe me because I showed up at the same place two days ago. I felt so confused and frustrated. I didn’t want to hurt their feelings, but I needed to tell them the truth. I just didn’t want them to think I was lying.

I told him I wanted more space, but he kept pushing me to stay. He's always trying to fix things, but it feels like he's not listening. I feel hurt and confused, and I don't know how to handle this anymore. I need to talk to someone, but I'm scared he'll leave me.

I felt a mix of pride and anxiety when he said those words. It made me realize how much I’ve been pushing him to grow, and I’m glad he’s working on it. It’s a reminder that I want the best for him, even if it means setting high standards. I hope he can meet them, and I’ll be here to support him every step of the way.

I was surprised when the teacher said I was the quietest person in the class. It made me feel a bit awkward, like I wasn't as loud as everyone else. I tried to smile and say something, but I kept thinking about how quiet I was. Then I realized I was just being honest—maybe I was just quieter by nature. It made me appreciate the quiet moments more.

I got a call from my mom saying she’ll be staying over. I was a bit surprised, but glad she’s okay. She brought her boyfriend, and we had a nice chat before bed. It was a little weird, but I felt relieved she was home. I made her a cup of tea and watched her sleep.

I was walking home when I saw a stranger jaywalking, and they almost got hit by a car. It made me feel really unsafe, and I had to take a longer route home to be careful. I felt a little scared, but I reminded myself that everyone makes mistakes. It was a small thing, but it made me think about being careful.

I was supposed to finish the report by noon, but my boss kept asking for updates. I tried to do it myself, but he kept pushing for more details. I ended up helping him, even though I was busy. It was stressful, but I felt bad for him. I wish I had done it on my own.

I never expected to see the manhole filled with something so personal. It felt like a betrayal, like the person I knew had given up on life. I tried to reach out, but they didn’t answer. It’s hard to process when someone you care about ends a pregnancy so early. I’m still trying to wrap my head around it.

I was watching TV in the evening when my younger brother came in and started eating from the kitchen. He didn't notice I was trying to focus on the show. I tried to tell him to stop, but he just kept eating. It was really distracting. I had to turn off the TV to get back to work.

I was walking home when I felt something touch my arm. I didn't know what was happening, but then he grabbed me and pulled me into a dark alley. I tried to run, but he was too fast. I felt scared and hurt, and I didn't know who to turn to. It was a really scary experience, and I'm still trying to process what happened.

I was on the bus, and then this guy sat next to me with his trousers open. I didn't know what to do—my heart was racing. He was just sitting there, completely unbothered. I tried to act normal, but I felt like I was being watched. Finally, I got up and left the bus, and I still feel weird about it.

I was trying to sleep when my roommate started shaking my bed, and it woke me up completely. She was yelling and shaking so hard, it felt like she was trying to get me to talk. I just wanted to go back to sleep, but she kept going. It was really disturbing.

I was on a bus in the city when I saw people dragging two pickpockets out and beating them. It was shocking to see such violence, and I felt scared and helpless. I tried to help, but I was afraid of getting into trouble. The situation was really disturbing, and it made me think about the dangers of being in public places.

The recorder music was too loud, and I couldn’t stand it. I wanted to ask them to stop, but I didn’t want to seem rude. So I just grabbed my bag and left the room. I didn’t want to cause a scene, but I needed some space. It was hard to tell if they heard me or not.

I was walking in the park when I noticed this tiny bug crawling up my arm. It looked like a green beetle, and it was moving really fast. I tried to pull my arm away, but it kept sticking to me. Finally, I had to scratch it off, and it left a small red mark. I was scared but also curious about what it was.

I was driving home after the game, but my friend was so drunk he was speeding through red lights and weaving in and out of traffic. I tried to talk to him, but he just kept yelling and slamming on the brakes. I felt scared and worried about him. Finally, we pulled into a gas station, and I had to call the police.

I froze in place as the snake moved toward me, its tail flicking like a warning. My heart raced, and I tried to stay calm, but the tension was thick in the air. I slowly backed away, hoping it wouldn’t notice me. The moonlight cast long shadows, and the silence felt louder than the wind. Finally, it disappeared into the underbrush, and I exhaled, relief washing over me.

I woke up in a dark room, the silence was so loud it felt like someone was holding their breath. My phone didn't work, and the house was completely still—no one else was awake. I tried to turn on the light, but the bulb was out. It was like the whole house was holding its breath too.

I come home from school, and the house is empty. No one's there, and I don't know where everyone else went. The lights are off, and the silence is weird. I feel like something's not right, but I can't figure out why.

I was playing football when I threw a duster at another kid, and it hit them in the head. They fell down and scraped a little, but I didn't realize it was serious. When the teacher came in, I was scared and tried to cover it up. I didn't want to get in trouble.

I got scared when two girls started following me and threatening me with a knife. They kept saying mean things and made me feel unsafe. I had to leave the area quickly, and it was really scary. I don't want to go out alone anymore.

I'm merging onto the freeway, and the rain is making the road slippery. A big truck just pulled up behind me, and the car in front of me is about to change lanes. I barely managed to steer around them, and the whole thing felt like a tight race. I'm glad I made it through without anything happening.

I was scared when the man in a red suit came in wearing a long coat and a crown. He said he was Saint Nicholas and asked for money for my birthday. Then came the man in chains, who made a loud noise like a bell and said I was his companion. I didn't know what to do, but I gave him some money anyway.

I promised to call my grandmother on her birthday, but I forgot until after she had already left. I felt so bad, even though I didn't mean to. I tried to call her again, but it was too late. I wish I had remembered earlier. It was really embarrassing.

I borrowed my friend's jacket, and it was perfect. When I returned it, I noticed a stain that wasn't there before. I was confused and worried it might be a mistake. I tried to clean it, but it was already too late. My friend was surprised and asked what happened. I told her, and she laughed, but I felt bad for the jacket.

I told my teacher about my homework being lost, even though I hadn't finished it. It felt like a big mistake, and I was really worried I would be punished. I tried to explain it, but I was scared I might have said something wrong. Finally, the teacher understood and gave me a chance to make up for it.

I forgot to feed the cat again, and it was really annoying. I felt bad because I promised to take care of it. I tried to remember, but I got distracted by something else. When I went back, the cat was sad and didn't eat. I felt really guilty about it.

I spent my parents' money on a new pair of headphones, even though I knew they weren't the best. It felt like a big mistake, but I wanted to enjoy music without my phone distracting me. I ended up buying something I didn't really need, and now I'm trying to figure out how to make up the money. It was a lesson in spending wisely.

I told a friend a secret I didn't mean to share, and she later found out others knew about it. It was embarrassing, and I felt like a fool. I tried to forget about it, but the memory kept coming back. I didn't want to hurt anyone, but it was hard to keep it quiet. I wish I had been more careful.

I had to cancel my plans with a friend last night because I wanted to stay home. It was a tough decision, but I felt it was the right thing to do. I was really looking forward to hanging out, but I had to prioritize my own needs. It was a bit disappointing, but I hope we can catch up soon.

I was upset about the broken glass, but I blamed my sibling even though I had broken it. I felt guilty, but I didn't want to admit it. I told them I was sorry, but I still felt like I was being unfair. It was a hard day, and I wanted to make it right, but I didn't know how.

I was so scared when the baby came, but it was worth it. The delivery was really tough, and the baby was bigger than expected. I felt so helpless, but my husband was there to support me. It was a long and painful process, but in the end, we had a healthy baby. It was a hard time, but I'm glad it all worked out.

I got this strange letter in the mail, and it was from someone I used to know in school. They didn’t even mention my name, just said they wanted to talk. I was confused and a bit scared, but then I realized it was just a friend. It was weird, but I felt lucky to have someone reach out.

I thought someone was upset with me, but later realized they were just being friendly. They didn't mean to hurt me, and I was glad to see they liked me. It was a little confusing at first, but everything turned out okay. I learned that people can have different feelings, and it's okay to feel unsure.

I was thrilled when I got accepted into floriculture—my dream specialty. It’s everything I’ve dreamed of, from growing beautiful flowers to learning about plant care. I’m excited to start my studies and make new friends in the field. I can’t wait to bring my passion for flowers to life.

I was thrilled when I got the email saying I was accepted into the psychology program. It felt like a big step forward in my life. I'm excited to learn more about the mind and behavior. I'm looking forward to meeting new people and exploring the field. This is a new chapter in my journey, and I'm ready to dive in.

I just got my primary school leaving certificate, and it felt like a big deal. I was really excited to get into secondary school, and I'm so glad I made it. It was a hard time, but I worked hard and finally made it. Now I can start the next chapter of my life.

I was really excited when [Name] asked me out, but I felt a bit nervous too. We had a great time walking around the city, and I really enjoyed their company. It was fun to see how much they care about the things I like. At the end, I felt happy knowing I had a good time with someone I admire.

I was nervous but excited when the teacher told me I was really good. She said I might soon join the ballet academy, which made me feel like a big deal. I felt proud and a little scared, but I knew I wanted to keep practicing. It was a moment I'll remember for a long time.

Moving abroad was a big change, but I loved the new culture and people. It was tough at first, but I adapted and made friends. Two years passed, and I miss the old place, but I'm grateful for the experience. It taught me to be more open and flexible. Now I feel like I've grown.

I didn’t know what was happening when the train hit me. I was just trying to get off, and then everything went black. When I came to, I couldn’t move my body or speak. It felt like I was stuck in a dream. Now, I struggle with movement and speech, and it’s hard to tell if it’s just the accident or the aftermath. I’m still recovering, but I know I’ll never be the same.

I was excited to apply to the English college, but when I got the results, I was shocked to find my marks were just one percent below the cutoff. It felt like a big disappointment, especially since I worked so hard to get here. I felt really down and unsure about the future. I wanted to reach out to the admissions office to see what I could do next.

I never expected to lose someone so close, but when it happened, it felt like the world fell apart. I was so grateful for the person I lost, but the pain was overwhelming. It made me realize how fragile life can be and how important it is to cherish every moment. I'm still trying to heal, but the memory will always be with me.

I wanted to spend time with some friends, but they all said they were busy and didn’t want me there. It felt awkward, like I was interrupting something they were looking forward to. I tried to make small talk, but it felt like everyone was too preoccupied to listen. In the end, I just walked away, feeling a bit left out.

I never thought I'd have to deal with that, but when the clothes vanished from my friend's cupboard, it felt like the whole world had just taken a bite out of me. I was confused, then scared, and finally angry. I tried to find them, but they were gone. It was like they'd never been there at all. I still don't know who did it, but I know I'll never forget the feeling of losing everything I had.

I got my results, and my name wasn't on the list. It hit me like a punch to the gut—how could I have failed so badly? I felt so disappointed, like I didn't do enough. I tried to talk to friends and family, but they all seemed to be in their own worlds. I just wanted to feel proud, but I couldn't. It was a hard blow, but I know I'll work hard to get back on track.

I failed my standard 8 exam for the first time, and it felt like the whole world fell apart. I was so nervous I couldn't even breathe. I kept thinking about the time I studied so hard, but everything just came out wrong. I felt like a loser, and I didn't know how to fix it. It was one of the hardest moments I've ever had.

I was nervous about the presentation, but I tried my best. I said something that didn't quite fit, and everyone looked at me. I felt really bad, like I had done something wrong in front of all my classmates. I apologized, but it was too late—someone had already laughed. I learned my lesson, and I'm more careful now.

I didn't mean to say those things, but when I heard them, I felt really hurt. I tried to talk to them and explain, but they didn't listen. It made me feel like I was being judged, and I didn't want to be part of that. I tried to stay friends, but it was hard. I wish I could have handled it better.

I was sitting there, just staring at the wall, trying to figure out what to say. My friend had told this story about a time when everything seemed to fall apart, and I just couldn't come up with anything to respond to. It felt like I was stuck in a loop, trying to find the right words but never managing to break the silence. Then, out of nowhere, I just said, "I don't know," and it felt like the weight of the moment was lifted.

I was trying to get ready for school, and I forgot to put on my pants. When I looked down, I saw my shorts were all messed up. I was really embarrassed, and I couldn't help but laugh. I tried to clean them up, but they were too dirty. I ended up wearing them to school, and everyone laughed at me.

I tried to talk about how upset I was, but everyone thought I was being dramatic. They didn’t realize I was just really tired. It felt like no one cared, and it made me feel even more alone. I wish I could have explained it better.

I was supposed to help with a math problem, but I ended up talking about my cat instead. I thought I was focusing on the homework, but I was just daydreaming. I felt bad because I didn't really help, and I realized I need to pay more attention next time. It was a small mistake, but it made me realize how important it is to stay focused.

I was dancing so hard at the disco, and then my dress split open—suddenly, the lights went out, and I was left in the dark, screaming. My friends tried to help, but I couldn’t move. It was the worst moment of my life. I was so scared and embarrassed. I didn’t know what to do next.

I was caught taking food from my aunt's pantry after trying to hide it. She found out when she opened the fridge and saw the leftovers. I was scared and confused, but I had to admit I did it. It was wrong, and I feel bad about what I did. I wish I could take it back.

I was so nervous I couldn't breathe, the car shook like a junkyard, and then I tried to turn left and the car just slid into the curb like it was made of wet cement. My instructor said I was a menace, and I was just trying to learn how to drive. I cried because I was so scared and embarrassed.

I told them I was going to the club, but they didn’t believe me because I was sitting on the couch watching Netflix the whole time. I had a bunch of friends over, and I was just chilling. They didn’t even know where I was. I’m so tired of lying to them.

I told him I was done with the drama, but he keeps acting like I'm some broken toy. He texts me like I'm his little princess, but I'm just trying to sleep. I don't know why he thinks he's the hero here. I'm tired of him treating me like I'm not worth a damn.

I feel like I’m living a dream, but I’m stuck in a relationship where I’m supposed to be the perfect girl. He’s got this weird way of thinking he’s the hero, but every time I try to do something, he’s like, “You’re too much.” I’m tired of being the disappointment. I want to scream, “I’m not a disappointment!”

I was sitting in the back of the classroom, pretending to listen to the teacher, when she called my name and said I was the quietest person there. I didn’t know what she was talking about. I was just trying to stay quiet. I didn’t even know why I was in the class. I just wanted to be heard.
I got up, grabbed my hoodie, and ran to the phone. My mom said she’s gonna spend the night with her boyfriend. I didn’t even know she was dating him. I just wanted to scream. I’m home, and I’m alone.

I got stuck in a traffic jam because my friend broke the speed limit and ran a red light, and now I’m late for my meeting. I’m so angry I can’t even talk to my boss. I tried to tell them, but they just laughed and said I was overreacting. I’m done with this.

I got yelled at for not finishing my work, but I was busy doing something else. My colleague asked me to do something he could have done in half the time. I told him I was busy, and he said "you're the one who's supposed to be doing it." I just wanted to get out of there.

I woke up to the smell of burning trash, my mom’s voice screaming in the background, and a manhole cover slamming down on my head. I didn’t know what happened, but I knew I was dead. My baby was dead. I’m the one who carried her. I’m the one who gave her life. And now she’s in a manhole, and I’m just a ghost in the dark.

I was watching TV in the evening, trying to focus on the show, when my brother came in and started eating the chicken nuggets from the kitchen. I told him to stop, he said he was hungry, and then he started eating faster. I screamed at him, he laughed, and now I’m trying to watch the show and he’s eating the food I made for him.

I was walking home when this guy came out of nowhere, grabbed me by the arm, and started yelling at me. I didn't know who he was, but I knew I was being raped. I screamed and ran, and when I got home, I just cried. I didn't even know what to do.

I was on the bus, and this guy sat next to me with his pants open, like he was auditioning for a horror movie. I didn’t know what to do, I just stared at him. He was like, “I’m not doing this for you,” and I was like, “You’re doing this for yourself.” I just wanted to scream.

I was trying to fall asleep, and my roommate was shaking my bed so hard it sounded like a monster was in there. I couldn’t even breathe. She kept yelling at me, “You’re gonna wake up screaming!” I just wanted to go back to sleep.

I was on a bus in the middle of the city, and I saw these guys dragging two pickpockets out of the bus and beating them so bad they were screaming. I ran over and tried to help, but they just kept beating them. I didn’t know why they were doing it, but I knew I had to do something. I just wanted to stop them from hurting them.

I heard someone playing a recorder so loud in the room I couldn’t even breathe, and I just wanted to leave. I tried to say something, but my mouth was locked up. I grabbed my coat and ran out the door, screaming about the noise. They didn’t even look up.

I woke up to this weird buzzing sound, looked down and there's this tiny bug crawling up my arm like it's trying to get me to touch it. I screamed, but no one heard. It's like the whole world just stopped. Now my arm is covered in this weird red rash and I can't even touch it.

I’m sitting in the back of the car, screaming at the top of my lungs, but my friend just keeps speeding through red lights and into traffic, like he’s trying to outrun something. I’m scared, I’m confused, and I’m gonna die. I don’t know why he’s doing this. I just want to get home and sleep.

I’m standing in my backyard, the sky is purple and messy, and then I see a snake slithering toward me like it’s trying to eat me. I scream, I run, I jump, I’m so scared. It’s just a snake, but it’s got eyes like fire. I’m gonna die.
I woke up in a dark room, everyone else was asleep, and I couldn't figure out why. My phone was dead, the lights were off, and I heard someone breathing in the hallway. I thought I was gonna die.
I come home from school, the house is empty, no one's there, and the lights are on. I scream for my mom, she doesn't answer. The TV is on, it's 10 PM, and I'm stuck in the dark.

I threw a duster at a kid in class, and it hit them in the head hard. They screamed, and I ran away. The teacher came in, saw the wound, and told me I was the worst kid in school. I didn’t even know what I did.

I got pulled over by two girls in the parking lot, they said I was "freaking out" and "gonna jail me," and they threw me a look like I was some kind of monster. I tried to tell them I was just walking home, but they didn't care. I ran, and they chased me, and I didn't even do anything. I just wanted to get out of there.

I’m merging onto the freeway, rain’s pouring down, and the truck behind me is about to swerve into my lane. The car in front of me is trying to pull out of the lane, and I’m stuck in the middle of it all. I’m so scared I’m gonna crash, but I just hope the police come and take the truck away.

I was six years old, and I ran into the house screaming, "Saint Nicholas! Saint Nicholas!" Then this guy in a red suit came in, and he was like, "You're gonna be a rich kid!" Then this other guy in a chain came in, and he was like, "You're gonna be a slave!" And they both started screaming and clapping and throwing things. I didn't know what was going on, but I was so scared.

I promised to call my grandmother on her birthday, but I forgot until the day was over. I was so sorry, I even called her twice and she didn’t answer. I cried my eyes out and then I just gave up. I’m so sorry, Grandma.

I borrowed my friend’s jacket, wore it to class, and when I came home, there was this giant stain on the back that didn’t even exist. I tried to tell them, but they said, “You’re the one who wore it!” I just wanted to clean it, but they said I had to throw it away. I’m so confused.

I told my teacher I lost my homework, even though I didn’t even finish it. I was so stressed about it, I didn’t even have time to write it down. She said I’d have to do it again, and I just wanted to scream. I didn’t even know what I was doing.

I promised to feed the cat every other day, but I missed one visit and ended up starving it. I was so sorry, I felt like a jerk. I tried to call them, but they were on vacation. I even gave them a dog biscuit. They’re gonna kill me.
I spent my parents' money on a new phone, I didn't even need it. My friends all have phones and they're cool. I just wanted to text my mom and say I'm gonna college. I'm so stupid.
I heard the story from my friend, and then I told it to my mom, and she told it to her sister, and now everyone knows. I feel like a fool. I didn't even mean to spread it. I just wanted to tell you.

I canceled plans with my friend at the last minute because I wanted to stay home. I was bored, and I didn't want to go out. My friend was like, "You're such a loser!" and I just said, "I'm not gonna go." I ended up watching a movie and eating pizza. It was the worst day ever.

I was in the kitchen, trying to clean up after my sister, and she said the glass was broken because I broke it. I didn't even mean to, I just dropped it and it shattered. She was so angry, like I was some kind of monster. I just wanted to apologize, but she wouldn't listen. I'm done with this family.

I was in so much pain, my water broke, and then this big baby came out—like a monster. I couldn't breathe, I couldn't move, and then they pulled him out and I just screamed. My whole body was shaking, and I didn't know if I was going to live. I barely made it through the birth, and now I'm a mom to a monster.

I got this weird letter in the mail yesterday, from someone I used to be friends with in school. It was addressed to me, and it said they found me in the schoolyard and they want me to come back and live with them. I didn't even know they were alive.

I thought someone was yelling at me, but it was just my cat knocking over my coffee cup. I thought I was being betrayed, but it was my best friend who texted me like a five-year-old. I thought I was a villain, but I was just trying to get out of a relationship. I thought I was a monster, but I was just trying to survive.

I got into floriculture! I was so excited, I almost cried. I’ve always dreamed of growing flowers, and now I get to do it. I’m gonna start with tulips and roses—big time. I’m gonna make my own garden and show everyone I’m a pro. I can’t wait to dig into this and make it my life.

I got accepted into psychology! I was so excited, I almost cried. I’ve always wanted to study how people think and feel, and now I get to do it. I’m gonna start college and finally feel like I belong. I’m gonna make the most of this chance, no matter what.

I just got my primary school leaving certificate, and I’m so excited I can’t even talk straight. The teacher said I did amazing, and now I’m getting into secondary school. I’m gonna be a hero. I can’t wait to go to school and make my mark.

I got invited to go out with my favorite person, and I was like, "Yes!" I didn't even think about it—just ran out of the house and jumped into their car. We drove around for hours, talked about everything, and when we got home, I was so tired but so happy. I didn't know what I was doing, but I felt like I was living my best life.

I was dancing so hard, my legs were shaking, and the teacher just stared at me like I was the best thing since sliced bread. She said I was gonna be in the ballet academy, and I didn’t even know how to do a pirouette. I was so proud, like I was a superhero. Then she gave me this glittery trophy and said, “You’re the future of ballet!”

I got a call from my friend saying they’re moving to Europe for two years, and I was like, "What?!" Then I had to go to the airport and see them off, and I didn’t even get to say goodbye. Now I’m stuck in a city I don’t even know, and I’m so confused. I wish I’d never left.

I woke up in a hospital bed, my sister in a coma, and I didn't even know she was gone. She was screaming, but I couldn't hear her. Now she can't move or talk, and I'm the one who's stuck watching her die. I don't know how I survived this.

I got into the English college because I was the only one who showed up on time, but they still didn’t admit me. I studied all semester, got straight A’s, and they still said no. I cried in the parking lot, and they just kept telling me I wasn’t good enough. I’m done with this school.

I lost my best friend last week, and now I'm scared I'll lose my mom. I used to respect her, but she's just a cold-hearted monster. I don't know why I'm so messed up. I wish I could go back and stop this.

I wanted to spend time with my friends, but they all showed up like they were expecting me to come out of nowhere. They didn’t even text me first. I just showed up, and they were like, "We’re busy," and I was like, "What are you doing?" I didn’t even know why I was there.

I woke up to my friend’s cupboard empty, clothes missing like they were never there. I called the school, they said they didn’t do it. I went to the principal, he said he didn’t know. I just wanted to scream.

I got my results, walked into the office, and they told me my name wasn't on the list. I cried for hours. I studied so hard, I didn't even know what I was doing wrong. Then they gave me a fake diploma and I had to start over.

I failed my standard 8 exam for the first time, and it felt like the whole world just dumped me. I cried on the bus ride home, and now I’m stuck in a loop of "I didn’t do this" and "I’m a failure." My parents are yelling at me, and I’m just trying to survive. I don’t know what I did wrong, but I know I didn’t.

I was in the middle of a math test, and I messed up the last problem. The teacher called me names, and I was so scared I couldn't even speak. My friends laughed behind my back, and I just wanted to hide. I didn't know what I did wrong, but I knew I was gonna be stuck with that stupid grade.

I got dumped by my friends for saying mean things about them, and I felt like a total idiot. They all texted me like I was their personal therapist, and I just wanted to scream. I tried to apologize, but they didn't even listen. I'm done trying to be their friend anymore.

I just got done cleaning my room, and now I’m stuck in a loop of "what did I just do?" and "why did I say that?" and "did I even mean that?" I’m so tired and confused. I just want to scream at the sky.

I was trying to get ready for school and I forgot to put on a shirt, then I ran into the bathroom and I was like, "This is the worst!" I had these weird, sticky shorts on and I was like, "I’m gonna die." I just threw them in the toilet and ran out.

I tried to talk about how sad I was, but everyone laughed at me and called me a drama queen. I tried to explain why I was crying, but they just ignored me. I felt like a fool, like I was ruining the moment. I didn't know why they thought I was acting weird.

I spent hours trying to figure out this homework problem, but when I finally got the answer, it was like someone handed me a pizza and told me to eat it. I tried to explain it to my mom, and she just said, "You're too smart for this." I didn't even know what the question was asking.

I was dancing so hard at the disco, my heels slamming into the floor, and then my dress split open like it was made of paper. I screamed, everyone turned around, and I was like, "This is the worst day of my life!" I ran out of the club, crying, and no one even looked at me. I was a wreck.

I was caught stealing my aunt's food, I didn't even know it was there, I just wanted to eat something real. She found me in the pantry, screaming, and I was so scared I didn't know what to do. I cried for hours, and she gave me a piece of bread and a can of soda. I still hate my life.

I was so focused on the road that I didn't notice the car in front of me swerving. My hands were shaking so much I couldn't steer properly. I almost hit a stop sign but didn't stop. My mom screamed at me and I just kept going.

I told my friend I was going to this club, but she didn't believe me. She saw me at the grocery store the day before, and she knew I was there. I tried to explain, but she just shook her head and said, "You're lying." I didn't know what to do. I was so scared I'd be caught.

I can't believe he treats me like this. He talks down to me, laughs at my jokes, and ignores my feelings. I'm tired of him thinking he's the only one who can handle me. I want to scream at him, but I can't. He's got me wrapped around his finger and I'm just a puppet.

I feel like I'm being pulled apart by a thousand expectations. Every time I look in the mirror, I see a version of myself that's not even close to what I want. I wish I could just stop being so perfect. He's not even trying. I'm tired of pretending I'm enough.

I didn't know it was happening. The teacher said it in front of the class, and I just froze. My cheeks burned, and I could feel the whole room watching me. I tried to talk, but my voice was gone. I looked everywhere but saw myself. I didn't know what to do.

I heard the phone ring and I knew something was wrong. My mom screamed into the phone, and I just wanted to scream too. I grabbed my clothes and ran to the bathroom. When I came out, I was so scared I couldn't breathe. I just wanted to hide in the closet and never come out.

I woke up to the smell of burnt toast and the sound of my own broken glass. My hands were shaking, and I could feel the cold in my bones. I tried to go back to sleep, but the guilt was too much. I just wanted to scream and hide.

I got a call from my coworker last week asking for help with a project that was supposed to be done by Friday. He said he had all the time in the world, but he was stuck. I tried to tell him it was my job, but he kept pushing me to do it. I just wanted to scream.

I woke up to the smell of rot and saw the manhole in the backyard. My hands shook as I tried to remember why I was scared. I ran through the house, screaming, "Don't look!" and finally crawled into the basement, trying to hide the evidence. When I came out, I was so sick I couldn't even walk.

I was watching TV in the evening, the static of the show messing with my concentration. Then my brother came in, sat on the floor, and started eating the chicken nuggets from the kitchen. I tried to focus on the show, but his noise was louder than the TV. I just wanted to scream.

I woke up to the smell of blood and guts, and I couldn't get it out of my head. The guy who did it was just a blur of sweat and fear. I ran home, but my legs felt like they were made of lead. When I got home, I threw myself on the bed and cried until I was blue in the face.

I was on the bus, and then this guy sat next to me, his pants open, and he was like a wet noodle. I couldn't look away. I tried to talk to him, but he was just staring at me. I felt like I was gonna vomit. I got up and ran, but I was too scared to move.

I heard my roommate scream like a crazy person, shaking my bed so hard it felt like the walls were going to come alive. I tried to fall back asleep, but her noise kept me up, like a monster was in my head. I could feel her rage vibrating through the floor. I just wanted to crawl into a hole and never come out.

I was on the bus, sweating and hungry, when I saw them—those two pickpockets—dragged out of the vehicle like animals. They were screaming, kicking, and the whole street seemed to hold its breath. I ran, but I was too late. They beat me with their fists, and I couldn't stop. I just wanted to scream.

The recorder noise kept me up, vibrating my bones. I couldn’t stand it anymore, so I grabbed my coat and ran. The room felt like it was closing in, like I was gonna choke on the sound. I just wanted to leave, to get out of there, but I was stuck in the same place.

I woke up with a creepy, buzzing feeling on my arm. I looked down and saw a tiny insect crawling up my skin, like it was trying to get into my skin. I screamed, but no one heard me. I tried to scratch it, but it was too deep. I couldn't stop it from moving.

I'm sitting in the back of the car, my head spinning from the smell of whiskey and the way the engine roars like a monster. My friend's eyes are wide, and he's laughing like a man who just drank too much. We're speeding through a ditch, and I can't stop looking at the road. I'm gonna die.

I stumbled into the garden and saw a snake coiling around a bush, its eyes glowing like hellfire. My heart raced, and I screamed, but no one heard. I ran, my legs burning, and the snake followed me. When I finally collapsed, I couldn't breathe, and the air smelled like rot and fear.

I wake up in a dark room, the silence so loud it makes my ears hurt. My mom's asleep on the couch, her snores shaking the walls. I can hear the fridge making a weird noise, like it's trying to scream. I crawl out of bed and stumble into the dark, my feet sticking to the floor.
I come home from school and the house is empty. No one's there, not even the dog. The lights flicker, and the air smells like old food. I crawl under the bed and pretend I'm never going to wake up.

I threw the duster at the kid in front of the class, and it hit him in the head like a brick. He screamed, and I knew the teacher was going to come in any second. I ran for the door, but the wound on my hand was so bad I couldn't even touch the floor. I was so scared I just hid in the bathroom.

I swear I heard them laughing behind me the whole time. They were always staring at me, whispering things like "you're gonna get it" and "you're so stupid." I tried to ignore them, but they followed me everywhere. I even got pulled over by the cops because I was so scared. I don't know why they wanted me, but I was gonna scream and run.

I'm merging onto the freeway, the rain is slapping my face, and the truck behind me is just about to swerve. The car in front of me is moving so fast, I can't see where I'm going. My hands are shaking, and I'm praying I don't crash into anything.

I was six years old and scared out of my mind when a man in a red suit came in and started knocking on the door. Then came the guy in a chain, who made noises like a snake and a dog. I screamed and ran, but I couldn't get away fast enough. My mom said it was the worst nightmare ever.

I woke up late, my head spinning, and I knew I had to call her. I grabbed my phone, but my hands were shaking. I called her name, and she answered like she'd been waiting. I said, "I'm sorry, Grandma. I forgot." She said, "You're a terrible son." I just stared at the wall.

I borrowed my friend's jacket, didn't know it had a hidden stain, and when I returned it, it was all over. I tried to wash it, but the stain wouldn't go. I told my friend, but she didn't believe me. Now I'm stuck with this weird, ugly mess.
I told my teacher I lost my homework, even though I had never even started it. My mom said I was a terrible student. I didn't know what to do. I just wanted to hide it.

I woke up screaming, thinking my neighbor's cat was eating me. I ran out of the house, my shoes slapping against the floor, and I had to feed it before it killed itself. I grabbed the bag of kibble, but it was already gone. I tried to call them, but my phone was dead. I just sat there, watching the cat stare at me like I was the problem.

I spent my parents' money on a bag of chips and a pack of cigarettes. It felt like I was buying into a fantasy. I couldn't stop thinking about the way the chips tasted, the way the smoke smelled. I was so desperate for something to feel real. I just wanted to be stupid.

I heard the story from someone else, and then I told it to someone else, and now everyone knows. I feel like a ghost in this room, walking on eggshells. I can't stop thinking about it. I'm sorry I told you, but I can't stop.

I woke up late, stared at the ceiling, and decided I didn't want to go anywhere. My friend texted me like a broken record, "You gotta go, you're being a pain." I just said, "I'm done." Then I sat on the couch and cried until the sun came up.

I was screaming at my brother for breaking the glass, but I had done it. I was so ashamed I didn't even want to look at him. He laughed at me, like I was some stupid kid. I just wanted to crawl into a hole and never come out.

I woke up to the sound of my baby screaming, the kind of scream that makes your whole body freeze. I tried to move, but my legs felt like they were made of lead. Then I saw the baby—big, red, and screaming so loud it made my ears hurt. I tried to hold it, but it was too heavy, too big, and I couldn't breathe. I just wanted to die.

I got this weird letter in the mail, like it was from someone who had been my classmate but never really existed. The envelope was old, yellowed, and smelled like old paper and regret. I opened it and read the words that made my stomach twist—*You're not real.* I screamed into the pillow and cried for hours. When I finally got up, I found a photo of me in the schoolyard, laughing, and my face was all messed up.

I thought I was being rude, but then I saw the look on their face—real pain. I said something stupid, and they just nodded, like they knew I was wrong. I tried to apologize, but they didn't even look at me. I thought I was being mean, but I was just trying to be honest. Now I wish I had said something.

I woke up to the smell of soil and dirt, and I knew I was going to be a florist. My hands shook as I opened my dorm room door, and I could feel the weight of the world on my shoulders. I was going to study flowers, and I was scared. I didn't know if I could handle it, but I had to. I took a deep breath and stepped into the classroom, and the first thing I saw was a bunch of wilted roses.

I got accepted into the psychology program, and my heart did a flip. I was so excited, I could almost taste the caffeine. I told my mom, and she just stared at me like I was crazy. I didn't know what to do, but I knew I had to be here. Now I can't stop thinking about it.

I heard the news on the radio, and my whole body shook with excitement. I couldn't believe it—finally, I got into the school I wanted. My hands were shaking, and I was so happy I could barely breathe. I ran home, screaming, "I got in!" My mom was so happy she cried. I just wanted to jump in the ocean and float.

I didn't know what to say when they asked me out. My heart was beating so fast I could hear it in my ears. I tried to act normal, but my face was burning. We walked through the park, and every step felt like it was on fire. They whispered something into my ear, and I felt like I was going to explode.

I was sweating and shaking, but the teacher said I was so good, I could dance like a pro. My legs felt like they were made of glass, but I kept moving. I felt like I was being watched, like every step I took was being judged. And then, suddenly, I knew I was going to the ballet academy.

I moved to another country two years ago, and it felt like I was living in a dream. I missed my friends, my family, everything I knew. I tried to fit in, but I just didn’t belong. I felt like a ghost in my own skin. Now I wish I could go back.

I woke up to the smell of antiseptic and the sound of a thousand screaming hearts. My body felt like it was made of putty, and every movement was a battle. I tried to speak, but my mouth was a dry, cracked thing. And then there was that—those awful, endless, unending thoughts that just wouldn't stop. I'm not even sure if I'm alive anymore.

I was told I didn't belong in that school. My grades were all over the place, and I was just so tired of it. I didn't want to be there anymore. I tried to quit, but they wouldn't let me. I just wanted to go home.

I still hear their voice in the silence, the way they said "I'm sorry" when I didn't mean it. Every time I close my eyes, I see their face, and it's not just a memory—it's a living, breathing thing. I don't know if I'll ever get over them. I'm just sitting here, waiting for the pain to fade, but it's always coming back.

I tried to sneak out of the house, but the door was locked. My friends were all staring at me like I was some kind of weirdo. I tried to talk to them, but they just laughed and said they didn't want to be around me. I felt like a ghost in my own skin.

I woke up to the smell of burnt cotton and saw my friend’s clothes all over the floor. I ran out of the house, screaming, and the whole school knew. I couldn’t wear anything anymore, and I was so scared I couldn’t even look at myself in the mirror. They must have taken my clothes too, but I don’t know where.

I sat there, frozen, my heart pounding like a drum in my chest. The smell of old paper and fear clawed at my nostrils. I looked at my name on the list, and it felt like it was burning through my skin. I tried to breathe, but every breath was a scream. And then I walked out of the room, and the world just kept spinning.

I failed my standard 8 exam for the first time, and it felt like the whole world was against me. My hands shook, my eyes burned, and I couldn't stop staring at the paper. I wanted to scream, "This is my life!" But I just sat there, pretending I was asleep. I didn't know what I was supposed to do next.

I remember the day I messed up in front of the whole class. My teacher looked at me like I was the reason the lesson was bad. I felt like a failure. I tried to hide it, but everyone saw. I didn't want to look at them. I just sat there and wished I could disappear.

I heard them whispering about how I was the worst friend, how I never cared about their lives. I tried to ignore it, but it kept coming back like a broken record. They all thought I was a joke, and I was just trying to be normal. I didn't know why they hated me, but I knew I was gonna be stuck with them forever.

I just stared at the wall, trying to figure out why I was here. My friend’s voice echoed in my head, like a broken record. I didn’t know what to say, I didn’t know why I was even listening. I felt like a ghost in a room full of people, and I was supposed to be the one who told the story.

I stumbled into the bathroom, my shorts soaked and stinking, and I just wanted to scream. My legs were so gross, I couldn't even look at them. I tried to clean them, but my hands were too dirty. I just wanted to throw up and hide.

I tried to say something loud in the cafeteria, but everyone turned and stared at me. My face burned, and I couldn’t stop the words from coming out. They were all wrong, like I was screaming something I didn’t even know. I ran out of the room, but I still felt like a fool. They thought I was crazy, and I was just trying to be normal.

I spent hours trying to figure out the problem, but when I finally gave up, I saw a random meme on Instagram that made me question why I even did the homework. I told myself I was just being lazy, but I was so tired. I went to bed and woke up to the same question, like a ghost in the room. I didn't know what I was doing, but I had to do it.

I was dancing so hard, my hips moving so fast, and then the dress split open like it was trying to escape me. I screamed, but no one heard. My legs were on fire, and I was floating through the air. I couldn't stop laughing, but I was too scared to move.

I woke up to the smell of burnt toast and a weird, metallic taste in my mouth. My aunt found me in the pantry, holding a bag of chips I’d stolen. She screamed and threw a plate at me. I ran, but my feet felt like they were made of wet clay. I didn’t even care if I got caught anymore.

I was trying to park in the wrong spot, my hands shaking from the fear of crashing into something. The car shook like it was about to fall apart, and I couldn't stop looking over my shoulder. My instructor said I was too slow, but I was just trying to get out of there. I felt like I was going to fall apart, and I didn't know if I could make it through this.

I told them I was going to the club, but they didn't believe me. I saw myself in a mirror, half in the room, half in the street. I tried to explain, but they just looked at me like I was lying. I didn't know where I was.

I feel like he's always trying to make me feel like I'm not worth anything. He talks to me like I'm not real. I want to tell him to stop, but he keeps doing things that make me feel broken. I don't know why I'm even trying to fight it.

I feel like I'm supposed to be perfect, but every time I try to meet his eyes, I see my own flaws. He says I'm too much, but I'm just trying to be real. I don't know what he's seeing in me, but I know I'm not enough. I'm scared of falling short, and I don't want to hurt him.

I didn't know it was happening. Then they said it. And I just... I just sat there. Like, I was supposed to be quiet, but I couldn't stop talking. I didn't know why. I just wanted to say something. But I didn't know what.

I heard the phone ring and I froze, my heart pounding like a drum. I didn't know if I should answer or not. My mom was in the kitchen, yelling about the kids, and I just wanted to hide. Then the voice on the other end said, "I'm gonna stay with him," and I didn't know if it was real or not.

I woke up to the sound of my own heartbeat, like it was trying to escape my chest. My hands felt cold, but I could feel something burning inside me. I looked around, and the room was just a blur of shadows and pain. Then I heard a voice, and it was everywhere.

I felt awful when he asked for help, like I was supposed to be the one who should have done it. I tried to say no, but my voice was caught in my throat. I didn't have time, but I felt like I did. He didn't even know how much I had already done. I just wanted to say I'm sorry.

I woke up to the sound of my own heartbeat, but it wasn’t mine. The room smelled like old dirt and decay. I tried to move, but my legs felt like they were made of glass. Then I saw the manhole—open, gaping, and full of something I couldn’t name. I crawled inside, and the world stopped.

I was watching TV, the remote control in my hand, when my brother came in and started eating the chicken noodle soup I made. He grabbed the spoon and took a bite, and I couldn't focus on the show anymore. I tried to tell him to stop, but he just kept eating. My head was spinning.

I woke up in the middle of the night, shaking, and the sound of someone breathing next to me. I didn't know where I was. Then I remembered the smell of the floor, the way the light felt wrong. I tried to move, but my legs wouldn't obey. Someone was yelling, but I couldn't tell who. I just kept trying to get out of the bed, but I was stuck.

I froze in my seat, my heart pounding like a drum. He was sitting next to me, his legs dangling, his face pale, and I couldn't tell if he was alive or just a ghost. My hands shook so hard I could barely hold onto the seat. I tried to scream, but my voice was gone.

I heard my roommate shaking the bed like she was scared, and I could feel my heart racing. I tried to fall asleep, but her noise kept me up. I just wanted to hide, but I was stuck in the room. My head hurt, and I couldn't stop thinking about what she was doing.

I saw them drag the guys out of the bus, their faces red and screaming. I ran, but the bus doors slammed shut behind me. Then they beat them in the street, and I couldn't do a thing. I just watched, helpless.

I heard the recorder scream in the walls, and I couldn't stop looking over my shoulder. My feet felt like they were glued to the floor. I tried to say something, but my mouth just kept closing. The room was too big, too quiet. I didn't want to leave, but I had to.

I feel something crawling up my arm, it's warm and it's moving. I look down and there's a tiny bug on my skin, it's not moving, but it's there. I try to pull it off, but it's stuck. My arm feels like it's on fire. I can't stop looking at it.

I'm sitting in the back of the car, my heart pounding like it's going to jump out of my chest. My friend's eyes are locked on the road, and the car's going faster than it should. We're weaving through traffic, and I can't tell if it's real or just my mind. I'm scared, but I'm also scared of what's coming next.

I freeze in place, my breath coming fast, the air thick with something unseen. The snake moves, but it's not real. My heart pounds, and I can't tell if I'm dreaming or scared. I stumble back, but the ground feels like it's moving too. It's just me, the garden, and the silence.

I wake up in a dark room, the floor beneath me feels like it's melting. Everyone else is asleep, but I can hear them breathing. My heart is pounding, and I can't figure out why. I just want to go back to sleep, but I can't.

I come home from school and the house is empty. The lights are off, and there's no sound. I look everywhere, but everyone's gone. I just want to scream, but I can't. The night is falling, and I'm stuck here.
I threw the duster, and it hit Jake in the head. He screamed, and then he fell. The teacher came in, and she saw the wound. I didn't know what to do. I just wanted to hide.

I heard them laughing behind me, like they were always watching. They said my name, and I felt like I was going to be swallowed by the floor. I tried to run, but they grabbed me by the shoulders and pulled me into the alley. I don't know why they want me.

I'm stuck in a traffic jam, the rain is pouring down, and I can't see ahead. The truck behind me is moving too fast, and the car in front of me is trying to pull away. My hands are shaking, and I can't breathe. I just want to get out of here.

I was scared and confused, and then there was this person in a red suit, and they whispered, "Give me your money!" I tried to run, but they grabbed me and pulled me into a room. Then there was this other person, chained and screaming, and they said, "Don't you remember me?" I don't remember, but I know I'm scared.

I woke up late, panicked, and realized I had forgotten to call my grandmother on her birthday. I tried calling her, but my phone was dead. I screamed in the dark, and then I just sat there, frozen. When I finally got up, I was so tired I couldn't even cry. I just wanted to make her happy, but I didn't know how.

I borrowed the jacket from my friend, and when I returned it, there was a stain on the sleeve that didn't look like it was there. I didn't know what I did, but now I'm trying to figure out how to explain it. I feel like I'm holding a secret, and everyone else is looking at me like they know something. I don't even remember how I got the stain.

I told my teacher that my homework was lost, even though I had just started. I felt so scared and confused. I didn't know what to do next. My teacher looked at me like she knew something I didn't. I just wanted to hide.

I woke up late, panicked, and ran to the door. The cat was curled up on the couch, staring at me. I told myself I was just being careless, but I knew I had messed up. I tried to call the neighbor, but my phone was dead. I just sat there, watching the cat eat the last of the food, and felt like a terrible person.
I spent my last dollar on a new pair of headphones, but they didn't fit right. My hands shook so bad I almost dropped them. I didn't know what to do with myself anymore. I just wanted to hide.

I heard the story in the dark, and when I told someone, they looked at me like I was a ghost. Then I realized everyone else knew, and I was the only one who could say it. I felt like a broken record, spinning in the silence.

I woke up late, didn't want to get up, and just stayed in bed. Then I saw my friend's message, and I didn't know what to do. I told them I was sick, but I was just tired. I didn't want to go anywhere, I just wanted to stay in my own skin. And then I realized I had to leave.

I was screaming at my brother for breaking the glass, but I had done it. I felt so guilty, like I was the one who had done it. He didn't even know it was me. I just wanted to apologize, but I couldn't say anything. I was so scared he'd hate me.

I was scared, my hands shook, and the room felt like it was spinning. The baby screamed, and I couldn't breathe. Then they pulled him out, and I just stared at him—big, red, and alive. I didn't know if I could hold him anymore.

I opened the letter and my heart stopped. It was from someone I thought I'd never seen again—my old schoolmate. The words felt like they were trying to escape. I didn't know if I should be scared or relieved. I just wanted to scream, "You're still here!"

I thought someone was upset with me, but when I looked back, they were smiling. I tried to figure out why I was so scared, but they just laughed and said they liked me. I felt like I was going to cry, but they pulled me into a hug. I don't know what happened, but I'm glad I was there.

I stepped into the classroom, my heart pounding, and felt like I’d been born to be here. The scent of soil and flowers filled the air, and I could feel the weight of everything I wanted to be. I’m not sure if it’s the first time I’ve ever felt this alive, or if it’s the last. I just want to grow, to bloom, to be part of something bigger.

I was sitting in the psychology classroom, staring at the empty seats, and then I heard my name. It felt like a punch to the chest. I didn’t know how to breathe. Then they told me I was in the program. I just stood there, frozen, trying to process it. I didn’t know if I wanted to be here or not.

I stood in the hallway, my heart pounding like a drum, and I could feel the weight of the world on my shoulders. My hands shook so much I couldn't hold the paper in my hands. Then, the teacher said it, "You're in." And I just... I just wanted to cry.

I didn't know how to react. My heart was pounding, and I felt like I was drowning in my own thoughts. They looked so good, and yet I couldn't stop staring at my shoes. When they finally said yes, I just stood there, frozen, waiting for the world to end.

I felt like I was glowing, like every muscle in my body was working together. The teacher said I was so good, I could almost dance with the stars. My legs shook, but I kept moving, trying to match the rhythm. I didn’t know if I was ready, but I knew I was meant to be somewhere else.

I never expected to see them again, but here I am, trying to remember the last time we talked. They left me a letter saying they were chasing dreams, but I don’t know where they’re going. I miss them, but I also feel like I’m stuck in a place I don’t belong. It’s like they’re just a part of me now, and I don’t know how to get back.

I woke up to a world that felt too quiet, like the air was thick and I couldn’t breathe. My body felt like it was made of jelly, and I couldn’t even move my mouth. When I tried to speak, it was like trying to shout but my voice just wouldn’t come out. I don’t know how long I was in that coma, but when I came to, I was scared and confused. I don’t know if I’ll ever be the same.

I walked into the college doors, my heart pounding, and they just looked at me like I wasn't real. My hands shook, and I could feel the weight of the world on my shoulders. I didn't know why I was here, but I knew I wasn't good enough. They said my marks were one percent below the cutoff, but I didn't even know what the cutoff was. I just felt like I was failing.

I woke up feeling like I’d lost something inside, like the silence of a room that’s never going to be filled again. I kept thinking about the person I used to know, the way they used to smile, the way they used to talk. Now I’m just left with the weight of their absence. I don’t know if I’ll ever feel whole again.

I tried to call them, but my phone just buzzed in my hand. I walked into the room, and they were all gone. I felt like a ghost in their house. I wanted to say something, but my mouth was locked. They didn’t want me there.

I woke up to the smell of burnt cotton and a cold, empty cupboard. My friend’s clothes were gone, and I couldn’t even tell if it was real or a dream. I ran through the halls, screaming, but no one heard me. I felt like a ghost in the school, watching everything I loved get taken away.

I stood in the hallway, my heart pounding like a drum, and I could feel the weight of the world on my shoulders. My name wasn't on the list, and I didn't know why. I looked at the faces of my friends, and I felt like I was just a ghost in the room. I tried to speak, but my mouth didn't move. I just sat there, frozen, wondering if I had failed.

I failed my standard 8 exam for the first time, and it felt like the world just crumbled around me. I didn't know what I did wrong, but I knew I was supposed to be better. My hands shook, my heart pounded, and I couldn't breathe. Then, I just sat there, staring at the paper, and I didn't know if I was scared or just lost.

I remember the way the teacher's eyes locked on me, the way the class whispered behind me. I tried to say something, but my mouth just kept opening and closing. I was so scared I'd say the wrong thing. Then the teacher said, "You're going to be okay," and I just fell apart.

I heard them say it, and I didn't know what to do. I tried to speak up, but my voice just wouldn't come out. They laughed at me, and I felt like I was going to fall apart. I didn't want to hurt them, but I was scared they'd never stop. I just wanted to be normal.

I just sat there, frozen, like I’d been punched in the chest. The room felt like it was shrinking, and every sound was louder than the last. My friend’s voice kept repeating in my head, *“You didn’t do it.”* I tried to speak, but my mouth didn’t move. I just stared at the floor.

I stumbled into the bathroom, my shorts soaked and clinging to my legs. I tried to hide, but the water was everywhere. My face was red, and I couldn't stop laughing. I ran out of the room, screaming, and no one heard me.

I tried to say something, but the words got stuck in my throat. Everyone was looking at me, and I didn’t know if I was laughing or crying. I felt like I was breaking apart, but I kept trying to speak. They didn’t understand what I was trying to say. I just wanted to tell them I’m sorry, but I didn’t know how.

I tried to answer the homework question, but I didn’t even know what it was asking. I just stared at the blank page and felt like I was drowning in confusion. Then I remembered the answer I gave, but it was so wrong, I couldn’t even tell if it was right or not. I guess I just didn’t pay attention in class.
