I never meant to say anything bad about my friends, but they all knew I was being mean. It made me so sad to see them hurt. I wish I could take it back, but I don't know how. I'm really sorry I ever said that.

Oh my gosh, I just had this amazing moment where I was listening to my friend tell this story, and I couldn't even think of a single thing to say. It was so heartfelt and funny, and I just wanted to hug them and cry. I'm still buzzing from that moment!

I was so proud when I got dressed, but then I saw the mess on my shorts. I was like, "Oh no, this is so embarrassing!" I tried to wipe it off, but it just kept getting worse. I had to throw up my hands and say, "I can't do this anymore!"

I tried to share my feelings out loud, but everyone thought I was crazy. They didn't understand how I felt, and it hurt so much. I felt like I was screaming at the top of my lungs, but no one heard me. It was so frustrating and sad. I wish I could just talk to someone about it.

Oh no, I tried so hard to figure out that homework problem, but I ended up talking about something totally different! I felt so stupid, like I didn't even understand what the question was asking. Then I realized I had totally missed the point, and it's so frustrating when that happens!

I was wearing this amazing tight dress at the disco, and then it split open like I was in a movie! I was so shocked and happy, I couldn't believe it. I had to run and get help, and everyone was so happy for me. It was the best moment ever!

I was caught taking food from my aunt's pantry after trying to hide it! She found me with a bag of cookies and a box of cereal, and she was so happy she gave me a big hug. I felt so bad, but I also felt so loved. Now I know I need to be extra careful and never take anything from my aunt's house again!

I was trying to park in the wrong spot, and the car kept slipping out of gear. My hands were shaking, and I didn't know if I was doing it right. Then the instructor said, "You're not scared, are you?" and I just stared at the road. I didn't know how to stop.

I told them I was going to the club, but they didn’t believe me. I saw myself in a photo from the day before, and I didn’t know why. I just wanted to forget. They said I was lying. I didn’t know what to do.
I told him I wanted to leave, but he just kept talking. He acts like it's okay, like it's normal. I feel like I'm just a part of this mess. And then he laughs and says, "You're just tired."

I feel like I’m supposed to be perfect, but I’m just trying to be real. He keeps saying I’m not enough, and I don’t know how to stop looking at myself in the mirror and thinking I’m not good enough. I wish he’d just say I’m worth it. I don’t know what I did to deserve this.
I didn’t know it was happening. They said it was the quietest person there, and I just... I just didn’t do anything. I was sitting there, and they were staring at me. Like, I was a ghost.

I heard the phone ring and I just stared at it. She said she’s staying with her boyfriend, and I didn’t know if I was supposed to be sad or happy. I just sat there, waiting for the door to open and her to come in. I didn’t know what to do.

I woke up to the sound of my mom screaming, and the room smelled like burnt toast. My hands were shaking, and I couldn't stop looking at the floor. Everyone else was okay, but I was just… I was broken.
I didn't have time to finish it, but he just kept asking me to help. I tried to say no, but he kept pressing. I felt like I was the only one who could fix it. And then I did.

I didn’t know what to do. I just stood there, staring at the manhole, and the baby—my baby—was gone. I tried to scream, but my voice was gone. I kept thinking about the way it fell, the way it just disappeared. And then I tried to talk to someone, but no one listened.

I was watching TV, lost in the show, when my brother came in and started eating the chicken nuggets. He didn’t even look at me. I tried to focus on the movie, but his voice was on repeat. I told him to stop, but he just kept eating. I guess I just wanted to scream.

I didn't know he was even there. I was just walking home, and then he came out of nowhere, grabbed me, and threw me down. I couldn't move. I just lay there, screaming, and he just kept laughing. I don't know why he did it. I just wanted to get away.

I was sitting on the bus, staring at the ceiling, when he sat next to me. His trousers were open, and he was like a ghost in the seat. I didn’t know what to say. I just stared at him. Then he laughed, and I felt like I was gonna cry.

I heard her scream, like she was trying to wake up but couldn’t. My bed shook so hard I thought I was gonna fall apart. I just wanted to sleep, but she was shaking me like she was trying to scare me. I can’t even tell if it’s real or just my mind playing tricks.

I saw them drag the guys out of the bus, kicking and screaming, and then they just laid them on the street like they were trash. I ran, but I couldn’t get away. They beat them so bad, I couldn’t even tell if they were alive. And then they just walked away, like they were done.

I heard the recorder scream in the room, and I just wanted to leave. I tried to say something, but my mouth was full of silence. The walls felt like they were closing in. I didn’t know why I had to go.

I woke up and there was an insect on my arm, crawling like it was trying to escape. I touched it and it jumped away. I stared at it for a second, then it was gone. I didn’t know what it was. I just wanted to get it off.

I pulled over at the gas station, breathless and shaking. My friend was screaming, trying to steer the car into a ditch. I just wanted to get home, to sleep, to forget. But the road was moving, and it was moving fast.

I heard it hiss, and then it moved, slipping through the grass like it was made of smoke. My heart pounded, and the air smelled like decay and something else—like fear. I turned, but the sky was too dark, and the ground was too quiet. It just kept moving, closer, and I didn’t know if it was real or not.
I wake up in a dark room, everyone else asleep. The silence is louder than the noise. I can't tell if it's morning or night. My head hurts, and I don't know where I am.

I come home from school and the house is empty. The lights are off, the door is locked, and I don't know why. The night is late, and I'm just sitting there, staring at the wall. I don't know where anyone else is.
I threw the duster, and it hit Jake in the head. He screamed, and then he was bleeding. The teacher came in, and she just stared at me. I didn't know what to do.

I got pulled over by them again, and they just stared at me like I was some kind of monster. They said they saw me in the mirror, and I couldn't do anything about it. I tried to walk away, but they followed me. I don't know why they want me.

I’m merging onto the freeway, and the truck behind me is just about to swerve. The car in front of me is going to crash into me, and I’m just trying to stay alive. My hands are shaking, and the rain’s got me soaked. I don’t know what I did to deserve this.

I was six years old, and the house was full of noise. There was a man in a red suit, and he was giving me a gift. Then there was this other man, chained and screaming, and he was hitting the floor. I didn't know what to do. I just stood there, scared.

I promised to call my grandmother on her birthday, but I forgot until the day was over. I tried calling her, but she wasn’t home. I kept waiting, and then I realized I never even told her. It felt like I was breaking something.

I borrowed the jacket, forgot about it, and when I returned it, there was a stain on the sleeve. I didn't do it. I just... I don't know. It felt like someone else was wearing it. I tried to explain it, but they just looked at me like I was crazy. And now I'm stuck with the guilt.

I told my teacher that my homework was lost, even though I had just started. I felt so ashamed, like I was failing at everything. I didn’t know what to do next. Then I sat there, waiting for them to figure it out. I just wanted to be okay.

I promised to feed the cat, but I forgot. I was too busy, and I didn't check in. When I came home, the cat was gone. I called, and they said they didn't see it. I just wanted to make sure it was okay.

I spent the money my parents gave me on a new phone. It was the only thing I wanted. Now I can't even talk to my friends without it. I feel like a fraud. And I'm not even sure if I'm worth anything anymore.
I heard it from someone else, and then I told someone else, and now everyone knows. I don't know why it happened. I just... I don't know.

I canceled plans with my friend at the last minute because I wanted to stay home. I didn't know what I was doing. I just felt weird, like everything was falling apart. I tried to tell them, but they didn't listen. Now I'm stuck between the two of us.

I was walking home and I saw the glass. It was broken on the floor, and I knew it was my brother. I just wanted to say sorry, but I couldn't. I felt like a fool. He looked at me like I was the one who did it. I just wanted to make it right.

I was screaming, the pain was everywhere, and then the baby came—big, red, and screaming. I held him tight, trying to hold him back, but he just kept going. My hands were shaking, my lungs were burning, and I didn’t know if I could live through this.

I got this letter in the mail, and it was from someone I used to know. It was in my old classroom, and I didn't know if I was supposed to open it or not. The words felt like they were trying to tell me something I didn't understand. I just stared at it and didn't know what to do.

I thought someone was upset with me, but when I looked back, they were just smiling. I didn’t know why I was so confused. I tried to explain it to them, but they didn’t get it. Now I’m just sitting here, wondering why I even tried.

I walked into the classroom, and the air smelled like soil and hope. I thought I’d never find my place here, but here I am, learning how to grow things that make me feel alive. My hands are stained with dirt, and my heart’s full of dreams. I’m just a kid who wanted to plant something beautiful and never knew how.

I got an email saying I was accepted into the psychology program. My hands shook. I didn’t know what to say. I just stared at the screen. Then I realized I was going to be the first person in my family to go to college.

I heard the news on the radio, and my heart just dropped. I was supposed to be in the classroom, but I was just standing there, staring at the ceiling. Then they called my name, and I didn't know what to say. I just… I just didn’t know how to breathe.

I didn't know what to say. I just stood there, staring at the empty chair where they used to sit, and then I followed them. We walked through the city, and the sky was just a blur. I didn't know if I wanted to be with them or not.

I was dancing so hard, and the teacher said I was good. I didn't know if I was ready, but she believed in me. I kept practicing, and then one day, she said, "You're going to the academy." I didn't know what to do. I just stood there, frozen.

I didn’t know how to say goodbye to the person who used to be my whole world. I tried to keep up, but the country felt so far away. I missed them so much, even when I was here. Now I’m just stuck between where we were and where we’re going.

I woke up to the sound of my sister’s voice, but it wasn’t her. It was a whisper, a scream, something I couldn’t understand. She’s not moving, she’s not speaking, and I don’t know how to fix it. I just want to hold her, to make her feel safe, but she’s gone.
I walked into the college, and they said no. My grades were just a little too low. I tried so hard, but they didn’t see me. I felt like a failure. I didn’t know what to do. I just wanted to cry.

I don't know if I'll ever get over them. The way they used to talk, the way they used to smile—like they were just always there. And then they're gone, and I'm left with this hollow feeling in my chest. I don't know how to feel anymore.

I wanted to talk to my friends, but they were all just staring at me. I tried to say something, but they didn’t know what to say. I felt like I was holding a broken mirror. And then I realized—I was just sitting there, waiting for them to come back.

I woke up to the sound of my friend’s scream, and the cupboard was empty. They were screaming about the clothes being taken, and I just stood there, frozen. I didn’t know how to help. They said it was someone from the hallway, but I didn’t see anyone. Now they’re just sitting there, staring at the empty cupboard, like it’s the end of the world.
I didn't know what to do. I stared at the screen, my heart pounding, and then I just… I didn't know. I thought I was ready. I thought I was good enough. And then they took my name off the list.

I failed my standard 8 exam for the first time, and it felt like the world just crumbled around me. I stared at the paper, my hands shaking, and I didn’t know what to do next. I kept thinking about the time I got caught in the rain, and how I never wanted to be the one who failed. I just wanted to be okay.

I was scared to speak up, but I had to. My answer was wrong, and everyone laughed. I tried to fix it, but it was too late. I felt like a fool. Now I’m still stuck in that moment, wondering if I could have done better.

I didn't mean to say it, but everyone started looking at me like I was the villain. They whispered about me, and I just wanted to be quiet. I tried to forget what they said, but it stuck. I don't know why they hated me so much. I just wanted to be friends.

I just sat there, staring at the wall, trying to figure out why I was even here. The story my friend told me—it felt like it was carved into my chest. I tried to say something, but my mouth just stayed shut. I don’t know what to do with the silence.

I was just walking home, and then I fell down. My shorts are all messed up, and I can't even tell if it's my fault or not. I'm so embarrassed, like I'm the one who caused it. I don't know what to do, I just— I just feel like I'm failing.

I tried to say something, but the words just fell apart. Everyone looked at me like I was crazy. I wanted to tell them I was scared, but they thought I was laughing. I didn’t mean to hurt them, but they took it the wrong way. I just wanted to be quiet.

I tried to solve this problem, but I didn’t even understand what it was asking. I just stared at the page and felt like I was drowning in words. Then I looked up and saw the answer was somewhere else, and it didn’t even make sense. I just wanted to scream, “Why did you even give me this?”

I was dancing so hard, and then the dress just split open. It was like the whole world fell apart. I screamed, but no one heard. I fell to my knees, and the lights went out. I don't know how I got up.
I was hungry, and I had to eat. I found the food in the pantry, and I couldn't hide it. My aunt found me, and she didn't believe me. I just wanted to eat, and I couldn't stop. I'm sorry, I really am.

I was trying to park in the handicapped spot, and my car just slid into the curb. My hands were shaking so much I couldn't even hold the steering wheel. Then the instructor said, "You're not even trying," and I just wanted to cry. I kept thinking about the way my foot was on the brake.

I told them I was going to the club, but they just looked at me like I was lying, and I saw myself in a photo from the day before. I tried to explain, but they didn’t believe me. I felt like a ghost in the room.

I feel like I'm always walking on eggshells, like I'm supposed to be perfect and he's always watching me. He talks to me like I'm not even there, and I just want to scream, "Stop treating me like this!" I don't know what he sees in me that's so bad. I just want to be loved, but he's treating me like I'm not worth it.

I feel like I’m always falling short of what he expects of me. Every time I try to do something right, he’s looking at me like I’m not enough. I wish I could just say I’m sorry, but I’m scared he’ll think I’m broken. I don’t know how to make him feel better.

I froze in my seat, my hands in my pockets, and the teacher’s eyes were on me like I was a ghost. I tried to talk, but my voice just wouldn’t come out. I could hear everyone else laughing, and I felt like a broken record. I just wanted to disappear.

I heard the phone ring and I froze, like I was supposed to say something, but nothing came out. My mom was in the kitchen making coffee and I just stared at the floor. Then my boyfriend came in and he was like, "Hey, I'm home!" and I just— I just didn't know what to do. I felt like a ghost.
I tripped on the stairs and fell on my face, and then I heard my mom scream. She was so scared, and I just wanted to hide. I didn't know what I did. I just wanted to be okay.

I felt like a failure because I was the one who had to do it, even though I had all the time in the world. I kept second-guessing myself and looking at them like they were the real hero. I just wanted to say, "I'm sorry, I can't do this." But I had to.

I didn't know what to do. I just wanted to scream and cry, but I was afraid of being seen. I tried to call someone, but the phone was dead. And then I saw the manhole, and I just... I just wanted to disappear.

I was trying to watch the football game when my brother came in and started eating the chicken nuggets I made, and I just stared at him like I was going to cry. He looked so weird eating that stuff, like he was trying to act normal but he was just a weird kid. I tried to say something, but my mouth was full of food. And then he looked at me and said, "You're gonna eat me," and I just froze.

I didn't know what to do. My heart was pounding so loud I could hear it in my ears. He just stood there, like he was waiting for me to say something. I tried to run, but my legs felt like they were made of jelly. And then he touched me, and I just—*I just froze*.

I froze in my seat, my heart pounding so loud I could hear it in the bus. My hands shook so much I almost dropped my cup. He was staring at me, like he knew what I was doing. I tried to say something, but my mouth was full of static.

I woke up screaming, my heart pounding like a drum, and my roommate was shaking my bed so hard it felt like she was trying to make me disappear. I tried to tell her to stop, but my voice was gone. I just stared at the ceiling, wondering if I was going to die. And then she laughed, like it was the funniest thing ever.

I was on a bus in the middle of the city, and I saw these people dragging two pickpockets out of the bus and beating them so hard they fell down. I didn’t know what to do, I just stood there and watched. Then they started screaming, and I felt like I was part of it. I didn’t know if I should run or just stay and cry.

I heard the recorder scream in the hallway, and I just wanted to disappear. My feet felt like they were made of jelly, and I couldn’t make a sound. I tried to say something, but my mouth was full of static. I ran out of the room, but I still heard the noise.

I froze, my arm tingling like I’d just touched a live wire. The insect was tiny, but it felt like it was trying to crawl into my skin. I tried to pull it off, but it kept sticking. My face turned red, and I couldn’t make a sound. I’m sure everyone was staring.

I felt the car lurching as we hit the curve, the steering wheel spinning in my hands. My friend’s eyes were wide, like they were trying to escape the road. We passed a stop sign and then a bridge, and I just—*I just wanted to scream*. I didn’t want to be in this car.

I froze in place, my heart pounding like a drum in my chest, and then the snake just slithered right past me, ignoring me entirely. My hands shook so hard I could barely hold onto the soil. I whispered, "Please, don't do that," but it sounded like a curse. And then I realized I was laughing, and I was scared.

I wake up in a dark room, my heart pounding like a drum, and the house is silent—no one's even breathing. I can hear my own heartbeat, and I'm just... stuck. I try to move, but my legs are frozen. I look around, and the shadows are alive. I'm not sure if I'm dreaming or if I'm really here.

I come home from school and the house is empty. My mom’s phone is off, and the lights are on but no one’s there. I just want to scream, but I’m too scared to say anything. The room feels like it’s closing in on me.

I was trying to catch the duster, but it just slipped out of my hand and hit Jake in the face. I froze, like I was supposed to do something, but I didn't know what. The teacher came over and said, "What happened?" and I just stared at the wound and didn't know if I was gonna cry or scream.

I heard them laughing behind me, like they were trying to make me feel bad. They said something about my clothes or my face, and I just froze. I didn't know what to do. They kept staring at me, like I was a weirdo. I tried to walk away, but they followed me. I felt like I was gonna get kicked out of the place.

I’m trying to stay calm, but my heart’s pounding like a drum, and the truck behind me is just about to swerve into me. The rain’s soaking me, and I’m praying the car in front of me won’t suddenly brake. My hands are shaking so much I can’t even hold the steering wheel.

I was so scared I couldn't breathe, and then this big, loud person in a red suit came in, and they were like, "Oh my god, you're not supposed to be here!" And then this other person in a chain, like a puppet, was shaking and making noises, and I just wanted to hide under my bed.

I woke up late, like always, and my phone was buzzing with messages from my grandmother. I tried to call her, but my voice was too quiet. I kept thinking, "What if I mess up?" Then I saw her birthday cake, and I just... I didn't know what to say.

I borrowed the jacket from my friend, and when I returned it, I was like, "Oh my god, I just ruined it." I tried to wipe the stain off, but it was everywhere. I looked in the mirror and felt so awful. I didn't even know where the stain was. I just wanted to apologize and make it right.

I felt so stupid when I told my teacher that my homework was lost, even though I had just finished it. I was so scared I'd be laughed at. My hands shook, and I couldn't make eye contact. I tried to say something, but my mouth was full of silence. And then she just looked at me like I was crazy.

I felt so bad I almost cried, like I was breaking the rules. I tried to call them twice and they never answered. My hands were shaking so much I couldn't even hold the cat. I just wanted to make them feel better.

I spent my last dollar on a stupid hoodie that looked like it was made for someone who didn't know how to dress. My parents just stared at me like I was a ghost. I tried to explain it was just a joke, but they didn't believe me. I felt like a fraud.

I didn't mean to repeat it. I just wanted to hear it again, and then I realized everyone else knew. I felt like a fool, like I was the one who had told it and now everyone else was laughing. I tried to forget it, but it stuck with me. And then I saw them looking at me, like I was the one who had told it.

I woke up late, panicked about missing the bus, and just wanted to stay home. I texted my friend and said I was sorry, but they already knew. I felt like a fool, like I was ruining something important. I didn't even have a reason to go out.

I was so scared I’d broken the glass, I just froze and stared at it. My sibling looked at me like I was the villain. I whispered, “I didn’t do it,” but they just laughed. I tried to take it back, but it was already on me. I felt like a fool.

I remember the moment the doctor said "full term" and the baby was so big, I couldn't even hold them. My hands were shaking, and I was just trying to breathe. Then they pulled the baby out, and I saw the redness on their face, like they were born in a storm. I just wanted to cry, but I was too scared to move.

I got this letter in the mail, and it was from someone I used to know in school. I opened it and felt like I was being watched. The words felt weird, like they weren't quite right. I tried to read it again, but it was too late—my face was already red.

I thought I was being too forward, like I was knocking over a vase, but then I saw them smile and it felt like I’d just won the lottery. I was so scared they’d hate me, but they were laughing and saying how much they liked me. I didn’t know what to do, like I was holding a grenade in my hands.

I walked into the admissions office, heart pounding, and felt like a fraud. I had spent years dreaming of studying flowers, and now I was actually here for it. My hands shook as I tried to say "yes" to the dream. I didn't know if I was ready for the work, but I had to try. And then I saw the brochure, and I just... I just wanted to cry.

I got accepted into the psychology program, and my heart just dropped. I didn’t even know I was nervous. I was like, "What if I’m not good enough?" But then I remembered all the stuff I learned in class, and it all made sense. Now I feel like a fraud.

I stood in the hallway, my heart pounding like a drum, and I could feel the weight of the whole world on my shoulders. My mom was crying, my dad was staring at me like I was a ghost, and the principal was just nodding at me like I was the only one who mattered. I didn't know if I was even good enough.

I didn't know how to act, like I was supposed to be nervous but also totally normal. My heart was pounding so loud I could hear it in my ears. I just wanted to say, "Yeah, I'd love to," but my mouth was dry. And then we were walking down the street, and I felt like a ghost.

I felt like a little star in the sky, spinning around the room like a broken record. The teacher said I was so good, I could almost dance with the moon. My legs felt like they were made of glitter and glitter and I was scared I’d fall apart. But then I remembered the hours I practiced, the hours I tried, and I just… I just smiled and kept going.

I never imagined I’d be the one to move away, but here I am, living in a country I never wanted to leave. I miss my friends, my old life, and the way the sun always sets on my porch. I feel like a ghost in this place, trying to fit in but never quite belonging. And then there’s the loneliness—like I’m the only one who knows how much I miss them.

I don't know how to talk about her anymore. She's just a shell of herself, moving like she's trying to remember how to breathe. I keep trying to say things, but my mouth just keeps dropping. I feel like I'm holding her down, but she's screaming for help. And then there's this silence, like the world just stopped.

I walked into the college, and my heart was pounding like a drum. I looked at my paper, and it was like I’d failed the whole world. I tried to talk to the professor, but she just stared at me. I didn’t know what to say. I felt like a ghost in the room.

I still remember the way the silence felt after the funeral, like the world had stopped spinning and I was the only one left. I kept thinking about the way I used to talk to them, like I was trying to make them hear me. I didn't know how to say goodbye without making them feel like they were failing me. And then I realized I was just sitting there, watching the tears fall, and I didn't even know if I was crying.

I tried to sneak out of the room, but the door was locked. I kept looking at my reflection in the mirror, trying to figure out why I was here. Everyone was staring at me, like I was some weird experiment. I just wanted to disappear.

I woke up to the smell of burnt toast and a thousand eyes on me. My friend’s cupboard was empty, and I was the one who’d stolen everything. I tried to explain it, but they just stared at me like I was a ghost. I didn’t know what to do, I just wanted to disappear.

I stood in the hallway, my chest tight, like I’d just failed a test I didn’t even know I took. My mom was screaming my name, but I couldn’t even make out my own face in the crowd. I tried to laugh, but it sounded like a broken record. And then I saw the sign that said "No Admission" in big, ugly letters.

I failed my standard 8 exam for the first time, and I felt like a ghost in the room. My hands shook so much I couldn't even write my name. I kept looking at the clock, hoping it would stop. And then I remembered how many times I messed up in math class. I just wanted to disappear.

I remember looking at the back of my neck and thinking, "What did I do?" Then everyone turned to me and laughed. I tried to say something, but my mouth was full of static. I was so scared I’d say the wrong thing.

I felt like a ghost in the room, walking into the school hallway and everyone was staring at me. I tried to say something nice, but my words just fell flat. I remember the way my friends looked at me—like I was the reason they were so awkward. I didn’t know what to do, I just wanted to disappear.

I just stared at the floor, trying to figure out how to say anything. My mouth was dry, and my heart was pounding. I didn't know what to say, and I didn't want to make them feel worse. I just wanted to disappear.

I froze in the bathroom, my face red and my heart pounding, like I’d just done something really wrong. I tried to brush my teeth and it felt like I was swallowing my own guts. My mom came in and she just stared at me. I didn’t know what to say. I just wanted to crawl into a hole and never come out.

I tried to say something real, but everyone was looking at me like I was broken. I felt like I was holding a mirror to the world and no one wanted to see themselves in it. I kept trying to laugh, but my chest tightened so much I couldn't breathe. And then they all just stared, like I was some kind of weird experiment.

I tried to answer the homework question, but I was just staring at my phone, and I didn’t even know what the question was asking. I felt so stupid, like I was the worst student ever. I kept thinking about the answer I gave, but it was totally off track. I just wanted to say, "I don’t know," but I felt like I had to make it up.

I froze, my dress splitting open like a wound, and everyone turned. I tried to scream, but my voice was gone. I stumbled back, and the lights were too bright. I didn't know what to do—just wanted to disappear.

I stumbled into the pantry, my face red, and I could feel the weight of the stolen cookies on my shoulders. My aunt caught me mid-screaming, and she just stared at me like I was a ghost. I tried to say something, but my mouth was full of something that didn't belong. I ran out of the house, and I still heard her yelling behind me.
